items.title: Dorothy Donegan — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I think playing with a band was something Mary Lou Williams could do better than me.

ctx.x: Well, tell me, did you play in any orchestras when you went to school?
I played in Roscoe Cotton’s band. But that didn’t last long. Because I think playing with a band was something Mary Lou Williams could do better than me.

items.title: Dorothy Donegan — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: She used to come in, she and Mary Lou, and they’d talk while I was playing.

ctx.x: I met her in Akron, OH.
Imagine that. She used to come in, she and Mary Lou, and they’d talk while I was playing.
Now, that’s an insult. Oh, sorry about that.
